correctness.rationale: For n=1,M=1,q~N(0,1),p=1/2 and z,rho>=0, the joint event is {-z<=q<=rho/z−z} whenever z>0. Its probability is Phi(rho/z−z)−Phi(−z), so the least feasible rho is g(z)=z[z+Phi^(−1)(1/2+Phi(−z))]. Origin (0,0) is feasible with P(q>=0)=1/2 and is handled separately: dividing by z there would be invalid. As z↓0, argument of Phi^{-1} ↑1 and g(z)/z→+∞; for any z0>0, the finite boundary slope g(z0)/z0 cannot dominate all secants from origin. Therefore some interpolation (tz0,t g(z0)) fails feasibility and the set is nonconvex. All constraints and p endpoint are allowed in the actual primary source. Proof is analytic, not numerical.
